deep.reconstruction:
The page holds one numerical table with no words or formulas. Column 1 is an argument x running from 9.60 to 9.94 in steps of 0.01. The form 9.xx is the usual 10-shifted tabular logarithm, so x is probably log a with a = 10^(x-10), roughly 0.398 to 0.871. This reading is my inference.

Column 2 gives integer values f(x), from 30119 at x = 9.60 to 177830 at x = 9.93. Most likely these are 5-decimal quantities scaled by 10^5. The row for 9.94 has no value.

Column 3 gives first differences, written between rows: Δ1(x) = f(x+0.01) - f(x), from 1497 to 11617. Column 4 gives second differences Δ2 = Δ1(x+0.01) - Δ1(x), from 79 to 1127. Horizontal rules every fifth line (after 9.65, 9.70, ..., 9.90) mark off blocks of five, the usual practice when building a table.

The point of the difference columns is to check and smooth independently computed values. Darker-ink overwrites show this was done:
- 54487 has its last digit rewritten.
- 2683 and 2839 are rewritten (the ink suggests earlier wrong digits).
- 156 and 164 are rewritten.
- 74244 has its last digit rewritten.
- 3793 is corrected (from 3798?).
- 4030, 221, 237 and 255 are retouched.
Gauss evidently found discrepancies in the differences and corrected the tabulated values.

The function is not named on the page. Its logarithmic growth rate d ln f/dx rises from about 4.85 near 9.60 to about 6.75 near 9.93. In terms of a, f/10^5 behaves roughly like a^2 times a slowly increasing factor (from about 1.90 at a = 0.398 to about 2.45 at a = 0.851). An empirical fit is f/10^5 ≈ 1.73·a^2·(1-a)^(-0.18). This is my own rough fit and does not identify the function.

The previous leaf is a bibliographic note (Fichte). The next leaf has a prescription and a separate log computation ("Decrem Logar. 0.3010300 = log 2", x = 0.0919983 / 0.9080017, y = 9.8581366). Any link to this table is speculative.
errors: No arithmetic errors. Every first difference equals f(x+0.01) - f(x), and every second difference equals the difference of consecutive first differences, as written (all 33 Δ1 and 32 Δ2 checked).

Third differences, computed by me, are irregular at the start: 3, 8, 2, 9, 4, 6, 10, 6, 7, 10, 12, 8, 13, ... The alternating fourth differences (+5, -6, +7, -5) suggest unit-level rounding errors in f near 9.62-9.65. This is within the last-digit uncertainty of a 5-figure table, so it is noise rather than a real slip.
The table stops at 9.93; the row for 9.94 is left without a value.
